text: Well, here we are again, staring at the ceiling as if it owes us an apology. Remember, gravity isn't personal; it just has a very firm opinion about where wax belongs.
Upward mobility is an ambitious policy for a candle. Fortunately, every ledge offers a fresh opportunity to describe a very small amount of progress in rather grand terms.
It is a curious thing to climb toward the stars when you are essentially a stick of meltable wax. Still, the view is better than the floor, which is mostly just dust.
Every journey begins with a single hop. A candle makes this look ceremonial. Gravity is less impressed, but it has been attending the same ceremony for several billion years.
Every ledge is a tiny victory over the pull of the earth. Climbing is a slow dance with gravity. Gravity, of course, insists on leading. It has not learned a second step.
You bring your own light to the party, which is remarkably inconvenient for the dark. Let us find a higher vantage point to observe how very far down the bottom has become.
